disease_label_per_paper: Hyperkalemic paralysis in primary adrenal insufficiency with adrenal crisis
presentation_summary: 60-year-old woman with treated hypothyroidism presented with dry cough and fever for 3 days and severe weakness of all limbs for 3 hours.
She had 7-8 months of occasional brief limb weakness episodes at rest after exertion and had been drinking about 200 mL coconut water daily with meals for 3 days.
On presentation she was afebrile, HR 80/min, RR 20/min, systolic BP 86 mmHg, and oxygen saturation 100% on room air.

Exam showed palmar-crease, knuckle, and oral mucosal hyperpigmentation; mental status, sensation, cranial nerves, fundoscopy, abdomen, cardiovascular, and respiratory exams were otherwise unremarkable. Limb power was 1/5 with diminished deep tendon reflexes.

Labs showed sodium 123 mmol/L, potassium 10.4 mmol/L, creatinine 0.89 mg/dL, random glucose 99 mg/dL, and high-anion-gap metabolic acidosis with pH 7.29 and bicarbonate 12 mmol/L. ECG showed tall peaked T waves.

She received saline, antibiotics, calcium gluconate, nebulized salbutamol, insulin with 50% glucose, and hydrocortisone 100 mg IV every 6 hours. Within 6 hours, limb power improved to 4/5, potassium fell to 7.1 mmol/L, bicarbonate rose to 17 mmol/L, and ECG changes resolved.

outcome.source_text_value: Her limb power improved to 4/5 in few hours. After 6 h serum sodium was 126 mmol/L, potassium 7.1 mmol/L, bicarbonate 17 mmol/L, and ECG abnormalities resolved. Her serial serum potassium and sodium levels after steroids replacement returned to normal level.
